title: Clicking a measurement end does not move it
goal: Clicking one end of a placed measurement, just to take hold of it, quietly changes the measurement. The end jumps under the pointer and the whole measuring line comes with it, so a reading you had lined up carefully is a different number afterwards and nothing tells you. A click that does not travel should leave the measurement exactly as it was.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-09 with a playtest walk on the probe build. A caliper was placed with the magnets off at feet (600, 500) to (800, 500), reading 100 px. One click at (795, 504), five points off the right foot dot, no drag: feet became (600, 504) to (795, 504), reading 98 px. Both ends moved and the number changed, from a click. Walk used: /tmp/foot-click.json (steps: open Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png, key i, distance mode, three command-clicks to place, key v, describe, click at [795, 504] with command, describe).

Why: the handle grab has about nine points of tolerance around the dot (Sources/Photonz/CanvasPointerDrags.swift, mouseDown, the measureHandleDrag branch) and seeds MeasureHandleDrag with current = the press point rather than the handle point. mouseUp then commits drag.params() unconditionally (same file, the measureHandleDrag branch of mouseUp), and params() puts the dragged foot at current and levels the opposite foot onto it. So a press that never travels still commits the press point.

The fix wants the same shape the caption drag already has a few lines below in mouseUp: it measures how far the thing actually travelled and calls onCaptionPlaceCancel() when it did not, so no history step is taken and the render settles back. A foot drag should do the equivalent, and the head/readout drag needs the same treatment since it commits the same way. There is now a moved flag on MeasureHandleDrag, set on the first mouse-moved event, which is most of the answer already.

Found while building holding-shift-while-dragging-a-caliper-end-keeps; it predates that work and was deliberately left alone there to keep that change small.
acceptance: A press and release on a measurement end with no travel leaves both ends and the reading exactly as they were
A press and release on the readout chip with no travel leaves the number where it was placed
Dragging an end still works exactly as it does now, including the shift hold and the magnets
No undo step is added by a click that changed nothing
A walk proves it: place a measurement, click one of its ends slightly off the dot, and read the feet back unchanged

log.note: REPRODUCED before touching anything: ran the walk from the notes on the probe build. Placed at (600,500)-(800,500) reading 100 px; one click at (795,504) with no drag gave feet (600,504)-(795,504) reading 98 px. Exactly as filed.

Adversarial review before building. Considered fixing the JUMP instead of the click (seed the feet with a grip offset the way the head already does with grabCross/grabAlong). Rejected for this task: the magnets read the raw pointer, so a grip offset has to be threaded through the whole snap branch, and acceptance item 3 says dragging must keep working exactly as it does now. The shortest thing that delivers the value is to stop committing a press that never travelled. Also checked whether a click on a handle should DO anything: no, the layer is already selected, taking hold is the whole point.

Built it. New pure type PhotonzCore/MeasureHandlePress decides when a press becomes a drag (2 view points, the same threshold the caption pill uses), with 6 tests written first. MeasureHandleDrag gained pressPoint; mouseDragged now sets moved from real travel instead of unconditionally, and previews nothing before the threshold so there is no jump-and-settle-back; mouseUp commits only when moved, otherwise calls the new onMeasureEndpointCancel. Same gate added to the Esc path (CanvasKeys) and to the tool-switch abandon (CanvasDisplay), which previously dropped a previewed drag without putting the render back.

Verified on the real app, not assumed. New walk Scripts/playtest/caliper-click-holds-walk.json: 1-placed 100 px (600,500)-(800,500); 2-foot-clicked unchanged; 3-chip-clicked unchanged, chip still (700,440); 4-jiggled (a 1 document point drag) unchanged; 5-dragged 150 px; 6-one-undo back to 100 px at the placed feet, so the three clicks left no steps to step over; 7-held shift lands (900,500) with the other foot fixed; 8-magnets a non-command drag still lands and commits. All five acceptance items pass.
No regressions: 5 caliper walks, 7 measure walks, 2 snap-hold walks and 3 redline walks all ok, and Scripts/test.sh is green at 5571 tests in 464 suites.

Adversarial review of the built thing found one roughness I could not fix here and reproduced it before filing: grab a foot 8 points off its dot and pull 6 points right and the foot moves 2 points LEFT (100 px becomes 99 px), because a foot jumps to the pointer instead of keeping its grip. Filed as a-measurement-end-follows-your-hand-instead-of-j at p2-normal with the walk and the output. Recorded in the audit's rough list too.
Audit written: queue/audits/2026-09-12-measure-click-holds.json, with a real window capture (Screen Recording was granted this run) at queue/audits/2026-09-12-caliper-click-holds.png.

A press on a caliper foot or its readout that never travels now commits nothing and takes no undo step. New pure MeasureHandlePress in PhotonzCore (6 tests, written first) decides when a press becomes a drag at 2 view points, the same threshold the caption pill uses; CanvasPointerDrags gates the preview and the commit on it, and the Esc and tool-switch paths use it too. Verified on the probe build with a new walk, Scripts/playtest/caliper-click-holds-walk.json: the bug reproduced first (100 px became 98 px from one click), and after the fix a foot click, a chip click and a one-point jiggle all leave it at 100 px with both feet unmoved, a real drag still reads 150 px, one undo steps straight back to the placed caliper, and the shift hold and magnets are unchanged. 5 caliper, 7 measure, 2 snap-hold and 3 redline walks pass; Scripts/test.sh green at 5571 tests. Audit queue/audits/2026-09-12-measure-click-holds.json with a real window capture. Follow-up filed at p2-normal: a foot still jumps to the pointer once the drag starts, reproduced (hand 6 right, foot 2 left). Commit 10e815e7, pushed.
